claims.text: Adding approximately 5 mol% Hf to ZrB2 produces a homogeneous (Zr,Hf)B2 solid solution.
The Hf-modified ZrB2 solid solution can attain full densification by reactive SPS at approximately 1600 °C.
High-temperature service causes nanometric HfO2 patches to form in situ at grain boundaries.
The HfO2 features enhance oxidation durability relative to conventional single-phase ZrB2 and prior low-temperature specimens.
The HfO2 features enhance resistance to liquid plating-metal corrosion relative to conventional single-phase ZrB2 and prior low-temperature specimens.
Reactive SPS under an inert atmosphere with a short dwell time is an applicable route for processing the Hf-doped material at approximately 1600 °C.
Hf lowers the activation barrier for densification during sintering.
Lowering the densification activation barrier permits full consolidation at a lower processing temperature.
Trace Hf acts as an oxidation stabilizer during high-temperature exposure.
Hf promotes formation of a thin, adherent HfO2 passivating layer.
The HfO2 passivating layer reinforces grain boundaries and thereby improves oxidation and liquid-metal-corrosion resistance.
The Hf-doped material will have high mechanical strength after sintering at approximately 1600 °C.
The Hf-doped material will exhibit significantly lower oxidation rates than both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and prior low-temperature specimens.
Previously reported lower-temperature specimens have suboptimal oxidation and corrosion resistance.
The proposed material is applicable to continuous oxidizing exposure and liquid plating-metal baths at 1200–1300 °C.
